question: May this repository publish NFL-derived numbers at all?
information_we_have: The NFL.com Terms (read 2026-11-13) state the Services may be used 'solely for your own individual non-commercial and informational purposes only' and that 'Systematic retrieval of data ... to create or compile ... a database ... is prohibited absent our express prior written consent.'
information_we_lack: A written licence, or written counsel opinion, covering republication of standings, schedule and injury-report data in a public web page.
decision_it_blocks: Whether any numeric NFL table on this site may be published in its current form.
suggested_way_to_discover: Take the one-page question to counsel: does quoting official standings/injury rows with attribution and no commercial use fall inside §1.3? Record the answer in COORDINATION.md before the next pack is merged.

question: What price is a strategy actually compared against?
information_we_have: The NFL's own release names DraftKings, FanDuel and Fanatics as 2026 official sportsbook partners and Genius Sports as the exclusive official betting-data distributor.
information_we_lack: A licensed archive of timestamped opening and closing prices, so that G02, G08 and G10 can be evaluated.
decision_it_blocks: Every performance gate: G02, G08, G10 and therefore the whole leaderboard.
suggested_way_to_discover: Decide between (a) buying a commercial odds archive, (b) restricting the project to no-price research, or (c) manual timestamped capture under a documented fair-use rationale. Nothing else can be graded until one is chosen.

question: Which inputs may the originated line use without importing an un-sourced coefficient?
information_we_have: Verified points-for/against per game for all 32 clubs, plus the 14-game Week 10 slate; the model self-consistency check shows the model mean total differs from the league's own points-per-game by a computed amount (see the Lines page).
information_we_lack: A fitted home-field-advantage value, a shrinkage factor, and a victory-margin distribution - none of which any official page in this pack supplies.
decision_it_blocks: Publication of any moneyline probability, and therefore strategy NFL3-ST-03.
suggested_way_to_discover: Fit HFA, shrinkage and margin SD on a licensed multi-season results file, then re-run the builder. Until then the two parameters stay at their declared neutral values and the moneyline column stays blank.

question: How stale is the official injury report, and when is it final?
information_we_have: The Week 10 report read on 2026-11-13 publishes Player / Position / Injuries / Practice Status / Game Status. Designations were populated for 3 of 14 games; the other 11 clubs had Game Status blank.
information_we_lack: The publication cadence and the final-designation deadline, and a hash-stamped archive so a decision can be audited after the fact.
decision_it_blocks: Any claim that a depth deficiency was known before kickoff.
suggested_way_to_discover: Capture the injury page three times per week (Wednesday, Friday, Saturday) with a SHA-256 of the parsed table and an ET timestamp; only the latest pre-kickoff capture may be used to justify a deficiency flag.

question: Which games does the official standings table actually include?
information_we_have: A completed Thursday 12 November game (Commanders 24, Giants 21) is published on nfl.com/scores, but the standings table still shows both clubs with their pre-game 9-game records (WAS 3-5-1, NYG 5-3-1).
information_we_lack: An official statement of the standings refresh cadence.
decision_it_blocks: Any model that mixes standings-derived rates with already-played Week 10 results.
suggested_way_to_discover: Either lag all inputs to the standings snapshot date, or wait for the standings to refresh; never mix a standings-derived rate with a result the standings do not yet contain.

question: Is a club depth chart an official statement of who will start?
information_we_have: Both captured charts say so themselves: Patriots.com says the chart 'is unofficial and is published by the writers of Patriots.com'; the Lions chart is an 'Unofficial Depth Chart Compiled by Lions Football Communications'.
information_we_lack: An official NFL source that defines a starter, or a club-signed gameday designation.
decision_it_blocks: Whether a '2nd string will replace the starter' statement can be presented as fact.
suggested_way_to_discover: Publish every depth-derived row with the club's own caveat attached to the row, and treat the deficiency score as a proposed ranking, not a measured quantity.

question: Which prop families are off-limits before we even model them?
information_we_have: The NFL release states partners will work together 'to prohibit wagers the league finds objectionable, including bets tied to officiating and injuries, along with those that can be knowable in advance or easily manipulated by a single person.'
information_we_lack: The operator-level list of which specific markets each partner actually restricts.
decision_it_blocks: Strategy eligibility: gate G11 rejects a family before any modelling happens.
suggested_way_to_discover: Keep G11 as a hard pre-filter and add the operator restriction lists when they are published; never model an injury-outcome market as a candidate.

question: What is the measured dependence between two legs of a parlay or same-game combo?
information_we_have: A method: paired residuals, Pearson/phi on a joint sample, slate-clustered interval, and a copula-free empirical joint. Eight correlations measured from official standings data are published on the Correlations page as a worked demonstration.
information_we_lack: Any measured dependence for an actual betting pair: no licensed paired residual history exists in the repo.
decision_it_blocks: Gates G07 and G09, and therefore every parlay and SGP strategy.
suggested_way_to_discover: Accumulate graded paired outcomes in the ledger first; compute rho only on a training window; never assume independence to make a price look better.

question: How do we know a result is skill rather than a short run of variance?
information_we_have: A working demonstration: an OLS fit of win percentage on net points per game over the 32 official standings rows, with R-squared, slope interval and per-team residuals published.
information_we_lack: Graded selections with slate identifiers so the same statistic can be computed for a strategy rather than for a team.
decision_it_blocks: Gate G10 and every leaderboard tier above Tier 3.
suggested_way_to_discover: Reuse the same estimator on strategy residuals, clustered by slate, and require the interval lower bound to clear zero before any reward.

question: How many graded selections before a number is publishable?
information_we_have: A declared floor (200 per family) and the reason for it: with ten strategies each tested, an uncorrected threshold produces false positives far more often than the nominal rate.
information_we_lack: Any graded selection at all: the ledger is empty.
decision_it_blocks: Gates G03, G04, G06, G07 and G10.
suggested_way_to_discover: Start the ledger with paper-graded (unbet) selections; the floor is about statistical power, not about money, so it can be met without placing a wager.

question: What constrains how many players can actually be active?
information_we_have: The NFL Operations CBA summary states the gameday active list rises to 48 (from 46) and that teams must have at least eight offensive linemen; the 14-team playoff format is also stated there.
information_we_lack: 2026 practice-squad elevation counts and injured-reserve return counts, which are not on that page.
decision_it_blocks: The roster-availability sanity check inside the depth model.
suggested_way_to_discover: Add the current-season roster rules page when captured; until then, treat the 48-player figure as the only sourced constraint.

question: Do 2026 rule changes affect any market we model?
information_we_have: The 2026 rulebook page lists the 2026 changes including 6-1-6, which permits the kicking team to declare an onside kick at any time during the game.
information_we_lack: The full text of each changed rule, and any official scoring or timing interpretation.
decision_it_blocks: Any total or special-teams market that a rule change could move.
suggested_way_to_discover: Read the specific changed rules before modelling totals, and record which market families each change touches.

question: Which NFL pack is the canonical one?
information_we_have: Four independent NFL dashboards are now published from this repository: docs/nfl/, docs/nfl-3b81013c/, docs/nfl-origination/ and this one.
information_we_lack: An owner decision naming one canonical pack per question.
decision_it_blocks: Which table a reviewer should trust when two packs answer the same question differently.
suggested_way_to_discover: Pick a canonical pack per question and mark the others 'Archived provenance' with a banner. Do not delete: each carries its own source register.

question: Which published source links no longer resolve?
information_we_have: nfl.com/official-nfl-rules/ returns the official NFL 404 page when fetched on 2026-11-13. It is cited by 71 rows across 20+ files in this repository, including live published pages.
information_we_lack: An owner decision to repoint or withdraw each citation.
decision_it_blocks: Whether any row citing that URL can be treated as verified.
suggested_way_to_discover: Repoint every citation to operations.nfl.com/rules-officiating/2026-nfl-rulebook, or to the specific rule section, and re-run the source checkers.

question: Does the URL printed in the README actually load?
information_we_have: GitHub Pages is served from main:/, so docs/nfl/ is live at /docs/nfl/. The README's https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own6/nfl/ returns GitHub's 404 page.
information_we_lack: An owner edit to the README and to the older handoff notes.
decision_it_blocks: A reader following the README link lands on a 404.
suggested_way_to_discover: Change every /nfl/ link to /docs/nfl/ and re-check after the next Pages build.

question: What does 'top performing strategy' actually earn?
information_we_have: A four-tier ladder whose rewards are research standing and publication priority only; no monetary prize is offered and none may be offered while the terms restrict commercial use.
information_we_lack: An owner decision on whether any non-monetary reward beyond publication priority is wanted.
decision_it_blocks: How the leaderboard is described to contributors.
suggested_way_to_discover: Keep rewards non-monetary and state that explicitly on the leaderboard page, as it is now.
